findings.evidence: Lines 409-423: the docstring text is identical to lines 438-443, but the statement at 419-423 is a three-fold conjunction ending in `∃ L, HasCauchyPVAt ... ∧ L.re = ... ∧ L.im = ...`.

findings.evidence: OnCurve.lean:38-40 vs. the hypotheses of `windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed` in RealIntegral/Basic.lean:73-79 (no `IsPwC1ImmersionOn`) and of `windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed_interior_crossings` at OnCurve.lean:480-483 (`h_imm : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b`).
findings.fix: Say the new theorem specializes to avoiding curves that are piecewise-C¹ immersions, and that `Basic`'s theorem remains strictly more general for non-immersed curves (while assuming integrability, which this one derives).
findings.issue: The module docstring claims that because `hγ_lip` is vacuous when `γ` never meets `s`, "this also reproves the avoiding case". It does not: `windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed_interior_crossings` additionally requires `IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b`, while `windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed` (RealIntegral/Basic.lean:73) only requires continuity on `uIcc a b`, differentiability off a countable set, avoidance, and integrability — no immersion. Neither theorem subsumes the other, so the stated redundancy is false and invites deleting the strictly more general avoiding-case result.

summary: The mathematics checks out: the PV real part telescopes to log‖γ b − s‖ − log‖γ a − s‖ (vanishing by closedness), the imaginary part is the ordinary real integral, and the boundedness/integrability at C^{1,1} crossings are genuinely derived, not assumed. Two docstrings state something the declaration below them does not.
